# Independent audit: fixed-normal transport and sharp parity loss


fixed-normal-cap-transport-collisions-and-sharp-parity-loss.md.
Its standard-library verifier reran successfully: 15577 exact checks.
The archived finite transport proof was also reread. No repair is needed.

In each parity the consecutive-interval coupling has distinct midpoint
targets: both lexicographic indices are nondecreasing along its positive
entries, at least one increases strictly, and lexicographic addition
preserves the strict increase. The source inequalities
a_z(s)>=pi G_r(s), a_w(t)>=pi G_r(t), together with monotonicity
and homogeneity of Phi, prove c_rk>=v_rk.

The same ambient affine functional puts the Minkowski midpoint of the
two actual traces inside the original target cap at (s+t)/2.
Different parities need not give disjoint sets, so the targetwise
maximum is necessary. The retained a_k(t) baseline, the exact collision
identity, and the bounds max_r Phi_r<=Q<=Omega and Q>=Omega/p
all follow without adding overlapping target masses.

A parity with zero positive t-tail is correctly omitted from Omega.
If it has a nonempty null t-trace, pairing one fixed point with each
positive s-trace gives distinct targets and the separate 2^(-d)
volume scaling. This is valid also for supporting traces and vertical
normals; absence and null nonemptiness are not conflated.

For the sharpness family, every defining simplex vertex belongs to
the mixed set, so the body equals its mixed convex hull. The oblique
functional z_1+x_1 has 0<=x_1<=1/2. At integer thresholds its cap
therefore agrees exactly, in volume, with the full fibers z_1>=q.
The point fibers on the outer base face have zero d-volume.

The unit-cube comparison has the stated factors:
the integral of (N-sum y)_+^d is d! N^(n+d)/(n+d)!.
Translating z_1 at thresholds 0,L,2L gives the three exact U
expressions. Every parity has a positive surviving tail, since its
least representative after translation has coordinate sum <=n.
The ratio bound simplifies exactly to
2^(-n)[1+(3n+1)/(2L+n+1)]^(n+d). Its explicit epsilon bound follows
from the finite binomial/geometric-series estimate with Dx<=epsilon/2.
Combined with the transport lower bound, this proves the exact limiting
coefficient 2^(-n), for every fixed n,d, and also for Q/Omega
regardless of the chosen lexicographic order.

The separate adjacent-box counterexample has exact cap tails
A,1/2,1 at the three specified thresholds. Both endpoint cuts are
proper, and the midpoint lies in the actual gap between the two
oblique support intervals. Thus aggregating before Phi has no positive
universal coefficient. This does not contradict the parity-resolved
bound, which omits the non-surviving large parity.

The note proves cap-mass bounds for one fixed normal, with no
candidate selection or maximum-depth assertion. That scope is
consistent throughout.
note: Mathematical discussion retained to expose corrections and limitations. This is not a verification run, accepted premise, or approval of the revised submission. Association follows explicit source-document references, not an inferred dependency.
